data.body: The job grants only `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`, but `scripts/pr_status_labels.py`'s `ensure_review_label()` creates the repository's `needs-review` label via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels` whenever it doesn't already exist. That endpoint requires `issues: write`; `pull-requests: write` only covers adding/removing an existing label from a specific issue/PR number, not creating a repo-level label. This same repository already encodes that exact requirement: `scripts/issue_triage.py`'s `apply_fallback()` calls the identical `POST /repos/{repo}/labels` endpoint, and its job in `issue-triage.yml` is granted `issues: write` specifically for it. Since `needs-review` won't pre-exist in any consuming repository (including this one), the first qualifying run (opened/reopened/ready_for_review from a non-writer author, or any changes-requested flip) will fail inside `ensure_review_label()` with `Resource not accessible by integration`; `main()` catches this and returns 1 before applying any label, so the feature never fires. Add `issues: write` here, and update the misleading comment above it, `docs/pr-status-labels.md`'s security-model/usage text, and the `test_token_can_only_read_contents_and_write_pull_requests` assertion that currently forbids `issues: write` — or pre-create the label out of band and drop the auto-create path.
